# `Copy`

`Copy` marks a type whose values may be duplicated rather than moved. It is **opt in**, and
granted in the type's declaration (a `declared` aspect):

```metel
copy struct Point { x: f64, y: f64 }
```

`struct Point derives Clone, Copy .{ .. }` is the same declaration, and [`extend Point: Copy;` is an error](#spec.ownership.copy.legality-3).

A type may implement `Copy` only if every one of its fields — or, for an enum, every payload
in every variant — is itself `Copy`. Fixed-size arrays and tuples are `Copy` when their
elements are.

`Option<T>` is `Copy` when `T` is, and `Result<T, E>` when `T` and `E` are: the standard library grants it in their declarations (`derives Clone(T), Copy(T)`, and `(T, E)`), so an `Option<i64>` is copied and an `Option<String>` moves.

**References:** `&T` is `Copy`. `&var T` is not — an exclusive reference must remain unique,
so it is moved or reborrowed rather than duplicated.

**Granted in the declaration.** `Copy` is [a `declared` aspect](../declarations/aspects/declaration-properties.md#spec.declarations.aspects.aspect-declaration-properties.legality-1):
`copy struct P .{ .. }` and `struct P derives Clone, Copy .{ .. }` grant it ([Declaration Clauses](../declarations/aspects/declaration-clauses.md#spec.declarations.aspects.declaration-clauses.legality-6)),
and an `extend P: Copy;` of a type with a declaration is an error. The standard library grants it to the scalars and
to the structural kinds. Whether a type may be duplicated implicitly is its author's statement: a type from another
module cannot be made `Copy` by its user.

**The `Clone` it requires.** `Copy` declares `Clone` as a derived super-aspect: a type that derives `Copy` also derives
[`Clone`](clone.md), in its own entry, and that `clone` is the representation copy. It cannot be written, and `T: Copy` proves
`T: Clone`.

**What an implicit copy is.** A place read in value position (`let b := a`, an argument, `return a`, a struct field, an
array element, a by-value `self`, a by-copy capture, and the same for a field `a.x`, an index `a[i]` and a dereference
`*r`) copies a `Copy` value and moves any other. The copy is the representation copy; no user code runs, so it is not
observable and the compiler may elide it. A generic body decides from the bounds visible at its definition:
`fun relay<T>(x: T) -> T { x }` moves even when instantiated with a `Copy` type, and the same read under `T: Copy` is a
copy.

<details>
<summary>Formal rules</summary>

##### Legality Rule {#spec.ownership.copy.legality-1}

A declared `Copy` implementation is legal only when every struct field or enum payload is
`Copy`; conditional implementations are considered under their declared bounds.

##### Legality Rule {#spec.ownership.copy.legality-2}

In a generic body, reusing a value whose type is a nominal application that mentions an abstract type parameter, when whether that type is `Copy` depends on a condition the analysis of a generic body cannot decide, is an error (`T0047`) naming the type. A type that is, or contains, a `dyn Aspect` is undecided in the same way, since the erased type is not known to be `Copy` or not. The use is never treated as a move: a later solver may decide the condition, and an accepted program must not change meaning when it does. A bound that decides the condition, or a reference and an explicit `.clone()`, avoids the error.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 58b51abc04d9a96abb3604f28b34f09b66dcaa36 -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.ownership.copy.legality-3}

A named type is `Copy` only through its declaration: `copy struct P .{ .. }` or `struct P derives Clone, Copy .{ .. }`. An `extend T: Copy;` of a struct, enum or record is an error with a fix-it that moves it into the declaration.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 7ff6bac2f3c159c0d57a74f61abbe3fcb3000089 -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.ownership.copy.legality-4}

The `Clone` of a `Copy` type is derived and cannot be written: a written `extend T: Clone` for a `Copy` type overlaps the derived impl and is an error (`T0015`), and its `clone` is the representation copy. A type that needs a custom duplicate is not `Copy`.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 58b51abc04d9a96abb3604f28b34f09b66dcaa36 -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.ownership.copy.legality-5}

For an instantiation `T<A>`, `T<A>: Copy` holds when every field's type is `Copy` there, and the type is not `Drop`. It is judged per instantiation, not as a bound on the type parameters, so `copy struct View<T> { r: &T }` is `Copy` for every `T`, while `copy? struct Wrapper<T> { v: T }` is `Copy` exactly when `T` is.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 8156f9b70d40f62450255e0a8c9ce9c1af2d21b4 -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.ownership.copy.legality-6}

A place read in value position is a copy when the place's type is `Copy` and a move otherwise. A copy leaves the original unchanged and independent of the copy. A borrow reads nothing.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 7ff6bac2f3c159c0d57a74f61abbe3fcb3000089 -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.ownership.copy.legality-7}

A generic body decides whether a read is a copy or a move from the bounds visible at its definition. Without a `Copy` bound a read of a value of a type parameter is a move, whatever the call site passes.

<!-- rfc.py:last_reviewed 7ff6bac2f3c159c0d57a74f61abbe3fcb3000089 -->

##### Legality Rule {#spec.ownership.copy.legality-8}

`T: Copy` entails `T: Clone`, in the checker and in the analysis of generic bodies.
